# Valentinian Sophia, Horos, Achamoth and Soter

<a id="valentinian-pleroma"></a>
## #0 — The fullness in conjunction

Sophia belongs to a world already articulated through conjunction. Her solitary desire disturbs that world; its response restores her place while leaving a passion outside the boundary. The telling then follows that excluded life through formation, the making of a cosmos, the growth of spiritual seed and an eventual return. Upper Sophia's restoration is an early event in a story whose lower world has still to come into being.

The [selected Irenaeus source](../../../../episteme/sources/classical-premodern-philosophy/irenaeus/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1.md#complete-selected-text) **sources** this whole. In the Preface, Irenaeus says he has read disciples' commentaries and spoken with some of them, especially members of Ptolemy's school. He also states his intention to refute them. The narrative below paraphrases the account transmitted in I.1–8 through the Roberts–Rambaut translation, with the complete Preface and I.1–21 retained in its source house. Its events are events in that reported cosmology. Irenaeus's accusations, his own theological rebuttals and the later variants remain identifiable voices within the transmission.

At the beginning stands Bythus, the Depth, also called Proarche and Propator. Ennoea, also called Charis and Sige, exists with him. After an immeasurable stillness, he deposits the intended emanation in Sige. She conceives Nous, the Mind capable of comprehending the Father, together with Aletheia, Truth. These four constitute the first Tetrad. Nous, also named Monogenes, joins with Aletheia to produce Logos and Zoe; Logos and Zoe produce Anthropos and Ecclesia. The resulting eight form the primary Ogdoad. Further generation proceeds through two branches: Logos and Zoe produce a Decad, while Anthropos and Ecclesia produce a Duodecad. [I.1.1–3](../../../../episteme/sources/classical-premodern-philosophy/irenaeus/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1.md#telling-01) **sources** the order and its names.

| Group | Conjunctions in the opening account |
| --- | --- |
| Primary Ogdoad | Bythus — Sige |
| | Nous — Aletheia |
| | Logos — Zoe |
| | Anthropos — Ecclesia |
| Decad, from Logos and Zoe | Bythius — Mixis |
| | Ageratos — Henosis |
| | Autophyes — Hedone |
| | Acinetos — Syncrasis |
| | Monogenes — Macaria |
| Duodecad, from Anthropos and Ecclesia | Paracletus — Pistis |
| | Patricos — Elpis |
| | Metricos — Agape |
| | Ainos — Synesis |
| | Ecclesiasticus — Macariotes |
| | Theletos — Sophia |

These are the opening thirty Aeons in fifteen conjunctions, or syzygies. Their names remain attached to their positions: Bythius in the Decad differs from the first Bythus, while Monogenes appears both as a name of Nous and as a member of a later pair. Generation has given the fullness an order and a plurality. It has not distributed the Father's knowledge equally among its members.

Nous alone comprehends the Father. He wishes to communicate that greatness to the other Aeons, but Sige restrains him according to the Father's will. Their desire to seek the first source thus precedes Sophia's crisis. Each quietly longs to behold the producer of its seed and contemplate the root without beginning. The youngest Aeon of the Duodecad presses that desire beyond the measure sustained by her conjunction. [I.2.1](../../../../episteme/sources/classical-premodern-philosophy/irenaeus/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1.md#irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1-q005) **sources** this shared desire before her particular movement.

<a id="valentinian-upper-sophia-horos"></a>
## #1 — Sophia reaches; Horos restores

Sophia seeks to comprehend the Father apart from Theletos, her consort. The passion is a reaching towards what exceeds her capacity: she strains further into the Father's depth and comes close to dissolution in his sweetness. Horos supports and restrains her. Through that encounter she returns to herself, recognises that the Father is incomprehensible and relinquishes the intention that arose from her passion. Her survival depends on a limit that can sustain what it bounds. [I.2.2](../../../../episteme/sources/classical-premodern-philosophy/irenaeus/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1.md#irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1-q006) **sources** this movement.

Irenaeus immediately introduces another version. In this telling Sophia attempts the impossible without her consort and brings forth an amorphous substance, a birth unlike herself. She first grieves over its imperfection, then fears that she too will end, and falls into perplexity over its origin and concealment. Turning back, she appeals to the Father; other Aeons, especially Nous, join the supplication. The account locates the beginnings of matter in ignorance, grief, fear and bewilderment. Its “others” marks a variant within the opening report: the amorphous birth and the near-dissolution should remain distinguishable articulations of the passion. [I.2.3](../../../../episteme/sources/classical-premodern-philosophy/irenaeus/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1.md#irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1-q007) **qualifies** the preceding sequence.

The report then describes the Father producing Horos through Monogenes, without a consort and in the Father's own image. Horos receives several names: Stauros, Lytrotes, Carpistes, Horothetes and Metagoges. His intervention separates Sophia's *enthymesis*—the intention or conception associated with her passion—from Sophia herself. Purified and established, she remains within the Pleroma and returns to her conjunction. Her enthymesis, carrying its passion, is excluded. Upper Sophia's restoration and the expulsion of this formless offspring are two consequences of the same separating act. Calling the outcast Achamoth later in the telling must not send the restored upper Sophia into exile a second time. [I.2.4](../../../../episteme/sources/classical-premodern-philosophy/irenaeus/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1.md#irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1-q008) **sources** that distinction.

In I.3.5, Stauros names the sustaining function and Horos the separating function. The same power establishes and divides. The boundary protects a differentiated fullness, yet the life placed outside it persists and will require a further response. The account has restored Sophia without completing the fate of her passion. [I.3.5](../../../../episteme/sources/classical-premodern-philosophy/irenaeus/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1.md#irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1-q012) **sources** the two functions; the two separate Horoi reported later under Valentinus belong to the variant account considered below.

<a id="valentinian-christ-spirit-soter"></a>
## #2 — Teaching, thanksgiving and the common fruit

The Pleroma responds to Sophia's crisis with a new conjunction. By the Father's providence, Monogenes produces Christ and the Holy Spirit so that the Aeons will not suffer a similar passion. Christ teaches the nature of their conjunctions and the Father's incomprehensibility. What Sophia tried to overcome through solitary extension becomes something the fullness learns together: the Father cannot be measured by the powers that proceed from him, while his disclosure through Monogenes makes knowledge possible within their order.

The Holy Spirit brings the Aeons to thanksgiving and rest. Their forms and dispositions become equal in the account's language; they cease their private striving and share joy in the Father. From that common state, each contributes what is most beautiful and excellent in itself. The Father approves, Christ and the Spirit concur, and the contributions compose Jesus, the Saviour or Soter, also called Christ, Logos and Everything because he comes from all. Angels are produced with him. [I.2.5–6](../../../../episteme/sources/classical-premodern-philosophy/irenaeus/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1.md#telling-02) **sources** the teaching and collective production.

This sequence distinguishes the earlier Christ from the collective Soter even though the latter also bears the name Christ. The earlier Christ teaches and will first give form to Achamoth; the Soter is the common fruit who will later complete another formation. Their functions become difficult to follow if every occurrence of “Christ” is assigned to one undifferentiated actor. Irenaeus's own summary at [I.3.1](../../../../episteme/sources/classical-premodern-philosophy/irenaeus/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1.md#irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1-q011) **qualifies** the names by distinguishing the prior Christ from the Saviour subsequently produced.

The Soter's common origin gives the Aeons' differentiated contributions a consequence beyond their restored rest. What they produce together can act towards the excluded passion. The fullness's recovery now opens onto the being outside its limit.

<a id="valentinian-achamoth-formations"></a>
## #3 — Achamoth receives form twice

Outside the Pleroma, the expelled enthymesis exists in darkness and vacuity, without form, like an untimely birth. This is Achamoth, the lower Sophia of the subsequent story. The earlier Christ extends beyond Stauros and gives her form according to substance, initially distinguished from formation according to intelligence. He then withdraws his power, leaving an odour of immortality. Achamoth seeks the light that has departed. Her attempt to cross back is stopped by Horos; her cry of Iao enters the account as an explanation of that name.

Desire persists after the light withdraws. Grief follows her failure to comprehend it; fear follows the prospect that life itself will leave her; perplexity accompanies both. She also turns towards the one who gave her life. The selected translation contains a tension here: after distinguishing substantial formation from intelligence, I.4.1 later speaks of her having form “along with intelligence.” The second formation remains explicit at I.4.5. [The whole paragraph at I.4.1](../../../../episteme/sources/classical-premodern-philosophy/irenaeus/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1.md#irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1-q013) **sources** both the initial distinction and the awkward later wording; neither is silently rewritten.

Her affects begin to acquire cosmic consequence. In the first account, tears give rise to liquid substance; the smile that sometimes accompanies the remembered light gives rise to what is lucid; grief and perplexity yield corporeal existence. Her conversion generates the psychic order, including the Demiurge. The alternation matters: sorrow does not exhaust her condition, because the memory of light can still make her smile. Irenaeus interrupts this report with mockery, eventually proposing sweat as an explanation for waters that are not salty. That sweat proposal is his own satirical contribution, not another event in Achamoth's cosmogenesis. [I.4.2–4](../../../../episteme/sources/classical-premodern-philosophy/irenaeus/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1.md#telling-04) **sources** the affective account and **qualifies** it by preserving the change of speaker.

Achamoth petitions the Christ who has withdrawn. He sends the Paraclete, the collective Soter, accompanied by his angels. She first veils herself before their splendour, then receives strength from him and meets his coming. He forms her according to intelligence and heals her passions. The healing does not simply erase everything that has happened: he separates the passions from her, combines and consolidates them into substrates capable of further formation. Passion supplies material substance; conversion supplies psychic substance. What had been an unformed affective condition can now enter a differentiated order.

Freed from her passions, Achamoth looks upon the Soter's angels and conceives spiritual offspring in their likeness. Spiritual seed thus has a different origin from the material and psychic substrates. The Soter's formation enables this new generation, while the angels supply the image through which it occurs. [I.4.5](../../../../episteme/sources/classical-premodern-philosophy/irenaeus/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1.md#irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1-q016) **sources** the second formation, the enduring substrates and the seed. These stages carry the story from exclusion to the conditions of a world; the Demiurge has yet to organise them.

<a id="valentinian-cosmogenesis"></a>
## #4 — A maker who does not know his mother

Achamoth now stands in relation to three kinds: the material derived from passion, the psychic derived from conversion, and the spiritual offspring she has conceived. Under the Soter's instruction, she forms the psychic Demiurge. Through him she begins to make the images of the higher realities. She bears an image of the invisible Father; he bears an image of Nous; the angelic order below images the Aeons. Her agency remains hidden from the maker she produces. [I.5.1](../../../../episteme/sources/classical-premodern-philosophy/irenaeus/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1.md#irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1-q017) **sources** this mediated creation.

The Demiurge separates and orders the substances, making corporeal things from what was incorporeal and fashioning seven heavens. He becomes their ruler, the Hebdomas or sevenfold power. Achamoth's dwelling lies above him, below the Pleroma, and is called an Ogdoad. This intermediate “eighth” is a dwelling and relation in the created order; the primary Ogdoad names the eight first Aeons. Paradise also receives a place in the report as an angelic power above the third heaven. The narrated universe contains distinct regions whose names can repeat without making them the same region.

The Demiurge imagines that he has made everything through his own agency. Achamoth has moved him without making herself known, and his declaration that there is no other God expresses his ignorance of what exceeds him. His ordering power is effective within its world, but he cannot yet give an account of its source. [I.5.2–3](../../../../episteme/sources/classical-premodern-philosophy/irenaeus/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1.md#telling-05) **sources** the heavens, the intermediate dwelling and the concealed maternal agency.

### The second account of affects and elements

I.5.4 gives a further differentiation of the passions. Fear issues into psychic beings; grief into the wicked spirits and the Cosmocrator, the ruler of this world. The report calls this latter power a creature of the Demiurge, yet allows it greater knowledge of what lies above because of their different substances. Hierarchical command and knowledge do not everywhere coincide.

The corporeal elements receive the following relations:

| Element in I.5.4 | Reported affective relation |
| --- | --- |
| Earth | Stupor or bewilderment, the more fixed condition |
| Water | The movement of fear |
| Air | Grief |
| Fire | Inherent in the three, as ignorance is inherent in the passions |

[I.5.4](../../../../episteme/sources/classical-premodern-philosophy/irenaeus/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1.md#irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1-q020) **sources** this account. It remains beside the earlier tears/liquid, smile/light and grief/perplexity/corporeal account. The story therefore offers more than one articulation of affect becoming cosmos. Fire's inherence also differs from a scheme assigning four entirely independent passions to four elements. Their differences belong to the selected telling and continue to constrain its later comparison with the native four-plus-two.

### The human being and the seed's formation

The Demiurge forms an earthly human from a substance described as invisible and fluid, breathes into it the psychic principle and subsequently clothes it with the sensible flesh figured as skins. The human is made in image and likeness through these different relations. Achamoth meanwhile places spiritual seed within the Demiurge without his knowledge, so that it can pass through him into the human soul. Embodied psychic life becomes the place in which that seed grows towards rational maturity. The human's body, psychic animation and spiritual seed thus carry distinct histories: earth, Demiurge and mother all remain active in the account. [I.5.5–6](../../../../episteme/sources/classical-premodern-philosophy/irenaeus/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1.md#telling-05) **sources** these anthropogenic stages.

The three kinds acquire different destinies. Material existence cannot receive incorruptibility; psychic existence can incline towards the better or the worse; the spiritual is formed and brought to perfection through knowledge. I.6 describes a saving embodiment composed to receive and bring these conditions to completion. It also reports claims that spiritual people possess salvation by nature, while psychic people require faith and conduct. Irenaeus uses those claims to accuse the teachers and their followers of licentiousness. His allegations remain his polemical testimony; they do not independently establish how every member of a Valentinian community lived. [I.6](../../../../episteme/sources/classical-premodern-philosophy/irenaeus/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1.md#telling-06) **sources** the reported distinctions and **qualifies** their historical use.

I.7.2 introduces a Christological telling held by “some.” A psychic Christ produced by the Demiurge passes through Mary; the Soter descends upon him as a dove. Spiritual seed from Achamoth, psychic Christ, specially fashioned body and descending Soter compose its fourfold account. The suffering belongs to the psychic Christ and bodily formation, while the Soter and spiritual seed remain distinguished from that passion. This marked variant supplies a particular relation between the higher saving powers and embodied events; it does not replace the earlier distinction between upper Christ and collective Soter. [I.7.2](../../../../episteme/sources/classical-premodern-philosophy/irenaeus/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1.md#irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1-q025) **sources** its actors and its “some.”

The ignorance of the Demiurge also changes. At the Saviour's advent he learns of what is above him and joins him willingly. He continues to administer the world and care for the Church in expectation of his appointed reward. Disclosure preserves a place for his agency while changing his understanding of its scope. The account of prophetic speech similarly distinguishes utterances arising through Achamoth, the spiritual seed and the Demiurge, instead of assigning all inspired speech to a single level. [I.7.3–4](../../../../episteme/sources/classical-premodern-philosophy/irenaeus/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1.md#telling-07) **sources** these differences of agency and the maker's learning.

<a id="valentinian-differentiated-restoration"></a>
## #5→0 — Bridal return and what remains outside

Consummation waits upon the formation of the spiritual seed. When it has reached perfection, Achamoth leaves her intermediate dwelling and enters the Pleroma. She joins the Soter as bride to bridegroom. The spiritual people relinquish their psychic souls, enter the fullness and become brides of the angels who accompany the Soter. The generation occasioned by Achamoth's sight of those angels now reaches its corresponding union.

Other beings receive other destinations. The Demiurge passes into the intermediate dwelling Achamoth has left, and righteous psychic souls rest there. Those souls do not thereby enter the Pleroma. Fire, hidden within the world until its appointed moment, consumes matter and finally itself. I.7.5 further distinguishes good and evil psychic lives while maintaining the spiritual/material/psychic account of humanity. The ending gathers some beings into higher conjunction, resituates others and destroys material existence. [I.7.1 and I.7.5](../../../../episteme/sources/classical-premodern-philosophy/irenaeus/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1.md#telling-07) **source** this differentiated restoration.

The ending changes how the earlier boundary is understood. Horos's exclusion did not make the lower passion inert: beyond the limit, Achamoth received form, generated seed and mediated a cosmos. Her return likewise does not carry every product of that cosmos into the same destination. The restoration of upper Sophia, the formation of lower Achamoth, the Demiurge's education and the seed's maturation each retain their own time and consequence.

The reported school reads these movements back through Scripture. The lost sheep figures Achamoth wandering beyond the fullness; the lost coin figures upper Sophia's restoration. Bridal language gives conjunction its scriptural expression, and the exposition of John's prologue unfolds the first Ogdoad through named relations. Irenaeus closes that exposition by assigning it to Ptolemy, while contesting the school's handling of the text. His comparison of their exegesis to rearranging a royal mosaic into a fox belongs to his refutation, followed by further rebuttal in I.9 and the Church's rule of faith in I.10. [I.8–10](../../../../episteme/sources/classical-premodern-philosophy/irenaeus/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1.md#telling-08) **sources** the encounter between the school's readings and the witness who transmits and opposes them.

<a id="valentinian-variants"></a>
### Variants that keep the selected telling situated

The surrounding chapters preserve disagreement within the family of teachings. At I.11.1, Irenaeus attributes to Valentinus a first Dyad of Arrhetus and Sige, two Horoi, and a different account of an expelled mother, Christ and the remaining shadow from which the Demiurge proceeds. Secundus differentiates the primary Ogdoad into light and dark tetrads and places the fallen power among the fruits of the thirty. Other teachers differ over whether the first principle has a consort and over the number and arrangement of primary powers. [I.11](../../../../episteme/sources/classical-premodern-philosophy/irenaeus/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1.md#telling-11) **qualifies** any claim that the opening sequence speaks for every Valentinian.

I.12 reports Ptolemy's followers describing thought and will as the Father's two affections, further accounts of simultaneous or reordered generation, and competing origins of the Soter: all Aeons, ten, twelve, Christ and the Spirit, or primordial Anthropos. The collective Soter of the main telling remains intact precisely because these alternatives are not added as successive episodes in his birth. The selected edition flags corrupt readings and uncertain identifications in this material. [I.12](../../../../episteme/sources/classical-premodern-philosophy/irenaeus/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1.md#telling-12) **sources** the differences; its uncertainties qualify historical reconstruction.

The Marcosian branch adds a distinct symbolic arithmetic. In I.15.1, Sige's revelation to Marcus explicitly adds two and four to make six, then quadruples six to make twenty-four letter forms. I.17.1 makes the four physical elements images of the Tetrad and combines their four qualities—heat, cold, dryness and moisture—with them as an Ogdoad. These operations belong to the reported Marcosian letter and cosmological correspondences; they neither supply a missing episode in Achamoth's passion nor establish Taylor's particular founding comparison. [I.15.1](../../../../episteme/sources/classical-premodern-philosophy/irenaeus/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1.md#irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1-q038) and [I.17.1](../../../../episteme/sources/classical-premodern-philosophy/irenaeus/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1.md#irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1-q039) **source** the two operations separately.

The selected context also contains different redemptions. I.21 describes bridal enactments, baptisms with different formulas, oil and water, teachers who reject sensible rites in favour of knowledge itself, and deathbed invocations for passage beyond ruling powers and the Demiurge. Knowledge dissolving ignorance and an ascent beyond local judgment are present, but no one rite represents every account. [I.21](../../../../episteme/sources/classical-premodern-philosophy/irenaeus/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1/irenaeus-1885-against-heresies-book-1.md#telling-21) **sources** these variations. The full I.13–20 context retains Marcus's reported revelation, numerology, exegesis and Irenaeus's allegations without converting them into a single expanded original myth.

<a id="valentinian-authorial-return"></a>
### The Offered founding comparison

The [Neumann whole](../../../archetypal-ground/neumann-images/WHOLE.md#neumann-hero-centroversion) supplies the essay’s shared archetypal structuration of differentiation, local authority and return. The admitted A19 comparison places the Demiurge’s effective but derivative office within that shared field at its stated Offered standing. The reported Pleroma and lower cosmos remain the telling’s own ordered regions. Irenaeus’s report, the English translation and Taylor’s later reception have distinct historical dates; no region in the cosmology becomes a geographical filing category or a chronological stage of Neumann’s sequence.

The [copula programme, IV.5 and VI.3](../../../../../quilt/copula-derivation-chain-and-resource-pools.md) **compares** Sophia's movement, Horos's limit and the Aeons' common contribution with the two accountings. [Q27's complete copula/ballein session and poly-daimonic programme](../../../../../quilt/27-07-26-QUILTING-FOR-FULL-ARGUMENT.md) **grounds** that comparison's developmental provenance: the first registers Sophia/Horos as a companion founding myth; the second asks how an ordered plurality of named powers acts within a more encompassing world. The source acquisition now supplies the particular telling that the programme called for. It does not make its proposed symbolic appointments ancient terminology.

The founding reading remains **Offered**. It takes Sophia's solitary reach as the image of a claim acting without its partner or backing; Horos's separation as a recovered distinction; and the Aeons' contribution to the Soter as a throwing-together which makes another formation possible. The native `0/1→4+2` comparison asks whether the formed four can disclose the two conditions implicated in their formation. Those two are not two more physical elements. The fuller source also distributes the formation across upper Christ, collective Soter, Achamoth and Demiurge; “Sophia with the Limit makes the elements” remains the programme's comparative compression, not a replacement account of who acts.

A13's corrected distinction keeps this comparison from making every act of separation a fall. Horos separates in order to sustain, and Sophia's conjunction is restored through that act. The Soter is produced through contributions whose distinct origins remain named. The whole therefore **returns-to** [A13 — Two Logics of Two](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A13-Two-Logics-of-Two-Dia-Syn.md) as a lived image through which cutting, conjunction and return can be compared. A13 owns the native derivation; the mytheme does not prove it, and the telling's material destruction cannot be silently converted into the native noncancelling return.

The Demiurge supplies a second, differently bounded return. He genuinely orders a world while mistaking the extent of his own knowledge; later disclosure alters that self-understanding without immediately abolishing his work. This relation **compares** with [A19 — Complex as Local Arbitration Regime](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A19-Complex-as-Local-Arbitration-Regime.md) and **returns-to** its distinction between local competence and a claim to whole-field jurisdiction. The comparison concerns the movement from hidden dependence through disclosure to a resituated office. It does not diagnose an ancient figure or identify Aeons with Jungian complexes.
